best_plan.name: p1
best_plan.rationale: p1 achieved the best observed quality, with only 1 count off the ground truth (relative_error 0.0714), while also being the cheapest executed plan at about $0.0070. Alternative prompts and larger models either reduced quality substantially or increased both cost and latency, so p1 had the best cost-quality trade-off.

cost_model_explanation: The cost model showed that the dominant expense was the sem_filter over the 120 reviews for taken_3, while the exact pre-filter on idx and the final groupby/project were essentially free. That guided me to keep the plan structure fixed, compare only semantic model/prompt variants, and favor the cheapest semantic option that still preserved accuracy; Google Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite was the lowest-cost useful classifier among the tested plans.

plan_codes.p1:
pipeline = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name, "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
pipeline.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "taken_3")
pipeline.sem_filter(
    "the review text expresses an overall positive opinion of the movie",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)
pipeline.groupby([], ["count"], ["reviewId"])
pipeline.project(["count(reviewId)"])
pipeline
